content:
# Sirach 44 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** Sirach 44 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 16

---

## Disagreement 1 — 44:1, "fathers" vs. "ancestors"

**EMET:** "our fathers in their generations"
**LOGOS:** "our ancestors in their generations"
**PNEUMA:** "our ancestors, generation after generation"
**Issue:** Greek paterōn = fathers, ancestors. EMET retains "fathers" as literal and traditional; LOGOS/PNEUMA prefer "ancestors" for gender inclusivity and accuracy. "Fathers" is the established RSV/NRSV tradition here.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "ancestors" as the more accurate term — the list that follows includes figures beyond literal fathers.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 44:2, "apportioned" vs. "allotted" vs. "gave"

**EMET:** "The Lord apportioned to them great glory"
**LOGOS:** "The Lord allotted to them great glory"
**PNEUMA:** "The Lord gave them great glory"
**Issue:** Greek edikasen = made righteous/allotted/decreed. "Allotted" (LOGOS) captures the sense of deliberate divine distribution; "gave" (PNEUMA) is too simple.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "allotted" (LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 3 — 44:2, "from the beginning" vs. "from of old"

**EMET:** "his majesty from the beginning"
**LOGOS:** "his majesty from of old"
**PNEUMA:** "from the very beginning"
**Issue:** Greek ap' aiōnos = from of old/from eternity. "From of old" (LOGOS) is the standard biblical idiom; "from the beginning" (EMET) is more absolute.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "from of old" as the most accurate idiom for ap' aiōnos.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 44:4, catalog structure

**EMET:** "leaders of the people in their deliberations and in understanding of learning for the people, wise in their words of instruction"
**LOGOS:** "leaders of the people in their deliberations, understanding men of learning for the people, wise in their teaching"
**PNEUMA:** "some led their people in council; some taught the people and showed good sense; some spoke with wisdom in their instruction"
**Issue:** PNEUMA breaks the catalog into separate "some" clauses, losing the list-within-a-list structure. LOGOS is most compact and preserves the structure.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 44:5, "musical tunes" vs. "musical melodies" vs. "musical melodies"

**EMET:** "composed musical tunes"
**LOGOS:** "composed musical melodies"
**PNEUMA:** "composed musical melodies"
**Issue:** Greek melos = melody, tune. LOGOS/PNEUMA agree on "melodies"; "tunes" (EMET) is colloquial.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "melodies."

---

## Disagreement 6 — 44:6, "endowed with strength" vs. "furnished with resources" vs. "men of substance"

**EMET:** "rich men endowed with strength"
**LOGOS:** "wealthy men furnished with resources"
**PNEUMA:** "wealthy men of substance"
**Issue:** Greek en ischui = in strength/power. "Endowed with strength" (EMET) implies physical power; "furnished with resources" (LOGOS) implies material wealth. Context = wealthy men living in peace.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "endowed with resources" as a compromise — retaining the sense of both.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 44:9, "as though they had not existed" vs. "as though they had never existed"

**EMET:** "as though they had not existed"
**LOGOS:** "as though they had never existed"
**PNEUMA:** "as though they had never existed"
**Issue:** Minor: "not" vs. "never." LOGOS/PNEUMA use "never" for stronger negation; EMET is more literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "never" — the stronger negation captures the pathos of absolute erasure.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 44:10, "men of mercy" — what does this mean?

**EMET:** "men of mercy"
**LOGOS:** "men of mercy"
**PNEUMA:** "men of mercy"
**Issue:** Greek andres eleous = men of mercy/lovingkindness. All three agents render identically. The contrast with the forgotten men of v. 9 is clear: these remembered men were characterized by mercy.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows all three: "men of mercy."

---

## Disagreement 9 — 44:11, "good things" vs. "good inheritance" vs. "good deeds"

**EMET:** "their good things will remain"
**LOGOS:** "their good inheritance will remain"
**PNEUMA:** "their good deeds live on"
**Issue:** Greek agatha = good things. "Inheritance" (LOGOS) interprets the "good things" as property/legacy. "Good deeds" (PNEUMA) interprets them as acts. EMET is most literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "good things" — the ambiguity (material + moral legacy) may be intentional.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 44:14, "bodies were buried in peace" vs. "bodies rest in peace"

**EMET:** "Their bodies were buried in peace"
**LOGOS:** "Their bodies were buried in peace"
**PNEUMA:** "Their bodies rest in peace"
**Issue:** EMET/LOGOS agree; PNEUMA's "rest in peace" sounds like a gravestone inscription (R.I.P.) — anachronistic resonance. Greek: en eirēnē etaphēsan ta sōmata autōn.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS: "Their bodies were buried in peace."

---

## Disagreement 11 — 44:16, "example of repentance" — is this right?

**EMET:** "an example of repentance to all generations"
**LOGOS:** "he was an example of repentance for all generations"
**PNEUMA:** "he stands as a model of repentance for every generation"
**Issue:** Greek hupodeigma metanoias = example of repentance. This is puzzling given that Enoch's tradition emphasizes righteousness, not repentance. All agents faithfully render the Greek as given. "Example" (EMET/LOGOS) vs. "model" (PNEUMA).
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "example of repentance" as the literal Greek, with a note that the tradition may be unique to this text.

---

## Disagreement 12 — 44:17, "perfect" vs. "blameless"

**EMET:** "Noah was found perfect and righteous"
**LOGOS:** "Noah was found blameless and righteous"
**PNEUMA:** "Noah was found blameless and righteous"
**Issue:** Greek teleios = perfect, complete, blameless. "Blameless" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) echoes Gen. 6:9 LXX (amemptos); "perfect" (EMET) has different connotations in English.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "blameless" — matching the Genesis LXX language.

---

## Disagreement 13 — 44:17, "compensation" vs. "ransom" vs. "means of rescue"

**EMET:** "he became the compensation"
**LOGOS:** "he was a ransom"
**PNEUMA:** "he became the means of rescue"
**Issue:** Greek antallagma = exchange, compensation, ransom. "Ransom" (LOGOS) has theological weight; "compensation" (EMET) is more literal; "means of rescue" (PNEUMA) is too paraphrastic.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "ransom" — the term has proper theological weight and the best English resonance.

---

## Disagreement 14 — 44:20, "tested" vs. "proved faithful"

**EMET:** "when he was tested he was found faithful"
**LOGOS:** "when he was tested he proved faithful"
**PNEUMA:** "when put to the test he proved faithful"
**Issue:** Minor: "found faithful" vs. "proved faithful." "Proved" implies the result was demonstrated; "found" implies discovery. Both accurate.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "proved faithful" as the more active formulation.

---

## Disagreement 15 — 44:21, triple promise structure

**EMET:** "multiply him like the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed like the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea"
**LOGOS:** "multiply him like the dust of the earth, and lift his seed on high like the stars, and give them inheritance from sea to sea"
**PNEUMA:** "multiply like the dust of the earth, rise up high as the stars, and inherit land from sea to sea"
**Issue:** PNEUMA drops the object "his descendants" in the second clause and changes third-person to vague infinitive. EMET/LOGOS are more precise.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS with "raise his seed on high like the stars" — "raise on high" is more elevated than "exalt" in context.

---

## Disagreement 16 — 44:22, "To Isaac also" vs. "Likewise to Isaac"

**EMET:** "To Isaac also he granted the same assurance"
**LOGOS:** "Likewise to Isaac he confirmed the same promise"
**PNEUMA:** "The same promise he confirmed to Isaac"
**Issue:** Greek kai Isaak = and to Isaac. The transition marker. "Likewise" (LOGOS) is slightly more formal; "also" (EMET) is more literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "Likewise to Isaac he confirmed the same assurance" — "assurance" (EMET) rather than "promise" for the nuance of sworn declaration.

---

*Total disagreements logged: 16*
